name: What is a Junior ADU (JADU) and how does it differ from a standard ADU?

mainEntity.name: What is a Junior ADU (JADU) and how does it differ from a standard ADU?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Junior ADU (JADU) is a specific type of Accessory Dwelling Unit, typically created within an existing single-family home. It must be no more than 500 square feet, include an efficiency kitchen, and have a separate exterior entrance. Unlike a full ADU, a JADU may share a bathroom with the main dwelling and doesn't require additional parking. JADUs offer a more cost-effective and less invasive way to add living space, often suitable for elderly family members, adult children, or as a rental unit, contributing to housing flexibility within existing structures.
acceptedAnswer.description: A Junior ADU (JADU) is an internal living space up to 500 sq ft with an efficiency kitchen and separate entrance, created within an existing home, differing from a standard ADU by size and shared bathroom potential.
